title: Sculpt tone network and proportional radius matrix for compact components
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current token set creates competing contrast anchors when density is reduced for compact surfaces (tables, dense forms, action bars). This leads to inconsistent visual weight across components and occasional accessibility regressions at small sizes.

Goal: Produce a cohesive ‘tone network’ — a small, well-documented subset of color anchors with explicit delta rules — paired with a proportional radius matrix tuned for compact modes. The output must be implementable by engineering via token keys with clear migration guidance and a minimal set of component overrides.

Deliverables:
- Canonical tone network: 6 anchored semantic tokens (bg-surface, bg-elev-1, bg-elev-2, fg-primary, fg-muted, accent) with exact hex/RGBA for light/dark and delta rules for hover/active states.
- Proportional radius matrix: 4-step radius scale (none, micro, small, medium) defined as percentages correlated to component height to preserve tappability and perceived density.
- Migration guide: mapping table from legacy tokens to new anchors, recommended fallback strategy for third-party components, and PR template for token rollouts.
- Figma kit: updated token page, component examples (button/table/form-row) in compact vs default mode.
- Regression test checklist: visual examples, AX checks (color contrast and focus outline), snapshot guidance for QA.

Non-goals: Rewriting the entire palette; this work targets compact-density surfaces and does not attempt to change data visualization palettes beyond a small anchor for charts’ backgrounds.

Acceptance criteria:
- All anchored tokens have >=4.5:1 contrast for primary text in compact sizes where applicable, and clear contrast rationale documented.
- Radius matrix maintains minimum clickable area and does not reduce hit targets below platform standards (44px for touch controls unless explicitly non-touch component).
- Engineering can toggle a single boolean flag (compactMode) to apply token overrides with no CSS specificity hacks.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Small visual deltas appear jarring in legacy screens. Mitigation: Provide progressive migration via CSS variable fallbacks and a canary rollout plan (Console beta org).
- Risk: Third-party components hardcode radii. Mitigation: include CSS variables and an audit task for high-priority components and extensions.

Rollout plan:
1) Finalize tokens and Figma kit (this ticket).
2) Publish package and RFC for engineering implementation (1 week).
3) Canary rollout to internal console pages with opt-in flag, gather metrics and qualitative feedback (2 weeks).
4) Gradual enablement for public rollout aligned to tokens-2026.1 release.

Links:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/placeholder/redwood-tokens-compact
- Migration doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/compact-token-migration
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/placeholder

Notes: keep token keys semantic (e.g., color.surface, color.surfaceElev1, radius.micro) — avoid numeric-only keys to encourage future delta rules (temperature, chroma adjustments).
